audit.whatIsWrong: The page rated the lane 7.5/10 and described it as losing from 6 onward, while Illaoi wins 57.02% over 449 games.
audit.why: Rumble bullies levels 1-2 with Flamespitter's 600-range cone and Electro Harpoon poke, but he has no dash and no hard CC; once Illaoi has Harsh Lesson on 4s, Test of Spirit and her R, he cannot decline the fight.
audit.corrected: Difficulty lowered to 5/10 and the mid/late prose rewritten to say Illaoi takes over from level 4.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both level charts gave Rumble 5 of 7 stages and Illaoi none, which the packet itself flags as a defect against a 57.02% win rate.
audit.why: Illaoi's spikes are levels 3-4 (Test of Spirit plus tentacles), 6 (R spawns a tentacle per champion hit) and first item (Iceborn Gauntlet's slow on a dashless target). The Equalizer is 130/105/80 and zones ground; it is not a duel answer.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Rumble, Rumble, Skill, Illaoi, Illaoi, Illaoi, Illaoi in matched full+content pairs with ratings and whys updated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said Rumble 'pillars away' and 'pillars out' twice, and wants.foe[1] credited him with a silence. Rumble has neither.
audit.why: Riot's text for Scrap Shield: 'Rumble pulls up a shield, protecting him from damage and granting him a quick burst of speed.' No terrain, no knockup - the kit file's terrain/knockup flags contradict the description. Junkyard Titan's Overheat makes RUMBLE unable to cast; it does not silence you.
audit.corrected: Pillar language removed and replaced with Scrap Shield's 6s speed burst; the silence line replaced with heat management, and the Overheat lockout named as your commit window.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is 6s flat, Harsh Lesson 4s, Test of Spirit 16s at rank 1, The Equalizer 130s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Those numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, the do/don't lines, the phases and the spikes so every 'wait for X' is concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: The missing-interactions entry claims Scrap Shield and The Equalizer deny Harsh Lesson's dash.
audit.why: That comes from the same misfiring terrain flag on Scrap Shield; Riot's text gives it no terrain and no grounding. The Equalizer creates a burning zone, not a wall that blocks movement.
audit.corrected: Not written to the page. Recorded here instead.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Scrap Shield's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your window: Harsh Lesson is 4s and he has no dash, so step in on Flamespitter and E him. Punish every Overheat lockout with a full commit.

edits.before: Leap of Faith inside your tentacle field is a 1v3 button. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Rumble's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Your R inside the tentacle field is a 1v3 button. The Equalizer is 130s at rank 1 and zones ground — step off the line and fight on.

edits.before: Iceborn Gauntlet is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Scrap Shield's cooldown.
edits.after: Iceborn Gauntlet is your spike — its slow pins a dashless Rumble inside the tentacle field.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — 6s shield plus speed burst; commit as it fades. - The Equalizer: 130s at rank 1 — step off the line. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 7.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Scrap Shield and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5/10. The lane is decided by how well you dodge Flamespitter's cone early and how disciplined you are.

edits.before: Tricky matchup — difficulty 7.5/10, Rumble carry threat 7/10.
edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 5/10, Rumble carry threat 7/10.

edits.before: Bait it, then commit. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Scrap Shield is 6s: shield plus a speed burst. Commit as it fades

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Sidestep the line; The Equalizer is 130s at rank 1 and then gone.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay even: he can pillar out but you can punish overheat with E.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are yours: Overheat locks him out of spells, so E him as he tips over.

edits.before: At 6 R Equalizer lets him zone your R field and win extended trades.
edits.after: At 6 your R adds a tentacle per champion hit and wins the extended fight.

edits.before: With his first item Rumble's uptime and shield juke your Tentacle slams.
edits.after: With your first item the slow pins him and your slams land on a dashless foe.

edits.before: Late, his AoE burn and R zoning dominate and he declines every slam fight.
edits.after: Late he cannot decline a sidelane duel and your field shreds his squishy build.

edits.before: This is your only real window: with W Harsh Lesson up you can W-gap onto him during his Flamespitter and force an E Test of Spirit before he pillars away, otherwise his heat combo out-pokes you all lane.
edits.after: This is your window: Harsh Lesson is a 4s cooldown, so step in during Flamespitter's 3s burn and land Test of Spirit. He has no dash to break away, only Scrap Shield's speed burst, so the spirit sticks.

edits.before: Rumble's R Equalizer is a lane-warping zone; stay off it, because he can drop the line over your R Tentacle field and out-damage your slams while kiting with E Electro-Harpoon slows.
edits.after: The Equalizer is 130s at rank 1 and a zoning wall, not a duel button — step out of the line and his answer is spent. Your R spawns a tentacle for each champion hit, so take the extended fight at 6.

edits.before: Even with your first item his Q Flamespitter uptime and W speed shield let him juke your Tentacle slams; you need a hard-CC jungle gank to convert.
edits.after: Iceborn Gauntlet's slow pins him inside your field: Rumble has no dash, so once you W onto him the tentacle swings land through Scrap Shield's 6s.

edits.before: Rumble's R zoning and AoE burn dominate team fights and he simply refuses to fight on your Tentacle field, so the raw matchup stays against you even as you scale.
edits.after: Late he cannot decline a sidelane duel — no dash, no hard CC — and a full tentacle field shreds his squishy build. Respect The Equalizer only in grouped fights.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are your best shot and read as skill — with W online you can gap-close during his Flamespitter and land E, but if he manages heat well and pillars out with his speed shield the window closes fast.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 read as skill — with W on 4s you can gap-close during his Flamespitter and land E, but if he manages heat well and kites out on Scrap Shield's speed burst the window closes fast.

edits.before: From 6 on Rumble reasserts control: R Equalizer zones your Tentacle field, his AoE burn wins extended fights, and he can decline any slam trade, which is why this stays a losing lane on paper despite Illaoi's teamfight scaling — punish only with jungle pressure.
edits.after: From 6 on you take over: your R adds a tentacle for every champion hit, Rumble has no dash or hard CC to break a W-gap, and The Equalizer on 130s is a zoning wall he cannot duel behind. Punish the seconds after he Overheats and cannot cast, then take the sidelane.

edits.before: Land E Test of Spirit the instant he overheats and loses his shield
edits.after: Land E Test of Spirit the instant he Overheats and cannot cast back

edits.before: Overheat-manage so his silence and shield are up for your all-in
edits.after: Manage his heat so he never Overheats into your all-in window

notes: Two real falsehoods killed: Rumble does not have a pillar (the page said he 'pillars away' / 'pillars out' - Scrap Shield is a shield plus a speed burst) and he does not silence you (Overheat locks HIS casting, which is your commit window). Kit-file derived flags on Scrap Shield ('knockup', 'terrain') contradict Riot's own description and were not used; same for the 'grounding'/'untargetable' flags on Illaoi's R. The level chart was flipped from Rumble 5/7 to Illaoi 4/7 in matched full+content pairs - the packet lists that contradiction as a defect. The mirror page (champ-data/content/rumble.js, illaoi entry) still carries the old chart, so it needs the inverse flips on rows 3-7 or mirror-fix.js will have to reconcile. Packet header disagrees with itself on volume: games 499 at top level, 449 inside the packet.
